filing_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
filing_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase disclosed that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card and entered a forward purchase commitment to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio, with closing expected approximately 24 months after December 30, 2025.
filing_evidence.summary: The 10-Q confirms a planned Apple Card portfolio acquisition and issuer transition to Chase.
filing_evidence.excerpt: On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card. The Firm entered into a forward purchase commitment on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio (the “Apple Card transaction”), with an expected closing date approximately 24 months thereafter.

filing_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
filing_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase reported $4.9 trillion in assets and $364.0 billion in stockholders' equity as of March 31, 2026.
filing_evidence.summary: The quarterly filing states JPMorganChase's asset and equity base at quarter-end.
filing_evidence.excerpt: JPMorganChase had $4.9 trillion in assets and $364.0 billion in stockholders’ equity as of March 31, 2026.

filing_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
filing_evidence.claim: At both March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, JPMorganChase's Advanced risk-based capital ratios were more binding than its Standardized risk-based ratios.
filing_evidence.summary: The filing identifies the binding capital regime for JPMorganChase at quarter-end.
filing_evidence.excerpt: At each of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, the Advanced risk-based ratios were more binding on the Firm than the Standardized risk-based ratios. Refer to Capital Risk Management on pages 33-40 of this Form 10-Q and pages 89–99 of JPMorganChase’s 2025 Form 10-K for additional information.

filing_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
filing_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase organizes management reporting into three reportable business segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management, with remaining activities in Corporate.
filing_evidence.summary: The filing defines JPMorganChase's reportable segment structure for investor analysis.
filing_evidence.excerpt: For management reporting purposes, the Firm has three reportable business segments – Consumer & Community Banking (“CCB”), Commercial & Investment Bank (“CIB”) and Asset & Wealth Management (“AWM”) – with the remaining activities in Corporate. The Firm's consumer business segment is CCB, and the Firm's wholesale business segments are CIB and AWM.

filing_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
filing_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase's principal bank subsidiary operates U.S. branches in 48 states and Washington, D.C., and the firm also operates through overseas branches, subsidiaries, representative offices and foreign subsidiary banks.
filing_evidence.summary: The quarterly filing describes the breadth of JPMorganChase's banking and broker-dealer footprint.
filing_evidence.excerpt: JPMorganChase’s principal bank subsidiary is JPMorgan Chase Bank, National Association (“JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.”), a national banking association with U.S. branches in 48 states and Washington, D.C. JPMorganChase’s principal non-bank subsidiary is J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (“J.P. Morgan Securities”), a U.S. broker-dealer. The bank and non-bank subsidiaries of JPMorganChase operate nationally as well as through overseas branches and subsidiaries, representative offices and subsidiary foreign banks.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: jpmc2026ccarresultsex99.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase's board intends to raise the quarterly common dividend to $1.65 per share from $1.50 for 3Q26, subject to customary board approval.
stress_test_evidence.summary: Planned dividend increase signals capital-return capacity following stress-capital update.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM) (“JPMorganChase” or the “Firm”) announced today that its Board of Directors intends to increase the quarterly common stock dividend to $1.65 per share (up from the current $1.50 per share) for the third quarter of 2026. The Firm’s quarterly common stock dividends are subject to approval by the Board of Directors at the customary times that those dividends are declared.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: jpmc2026ccarresultsex99.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase authorized a new $50 billion common share repurchase program effective July 1, 2026, with execution at management discretion.
stress_test_evidence.summary: A large buyback authorization provides flexibility for shareholder capital returns.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: In addition, the Firm’s Board of Directors has authorized a new common share repurchase program of $50 billion, effective July 1, 2026. The authorization to repurchase common shares will be used at management’s discretion, and the amount and timing of common share repurchases under the new authorization will be subject to various factors.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: jpmc2026ccarresultsex99.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: The Federal Reserve's February 2026 announcement left JPMorganChase's 2.5% Stress Capital Buffer requirement unchanged through September 30, 2027.
stress_test_evidence.summary: SCB stability reduces near-term uncertainty around regulatory capital requirements.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: Following the Federal Reserve’s announcement in February 2026, the Firm’s current Stress Capital Buffer (“SCB”) requirement of 2.5% will remain unchanged through September 30, 2027, with new requirements to be calculated in 2027 based on revised supervisory stress testing models that incorporate public feedback.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: jpmc2026ccarresultsex99.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase disclosed that its current standardized CET1 capital ratio requirement, including regulatory buffers, remains 11.5%.
stress_test_evidence.summary: The filing states the applicable standardized CET1 requirement including buffers.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: As a result, the Firm’s current Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 (“CET1”) capital ratio requirement including regulatory buffers continues to be 11.5%.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: jpmc2026ccarresultsex99.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: Management attributed the dividend increase and repurchase authorization to excess capital, liquidity, strong financial performance, and flexibility to enhance shareholder value, while acknowledging a complex risk environment.
stress_test_evidence.summary: CEO commentary is constructive on capital strength but flags elevated complexity of risks.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorganChase said: “Our fortress balance sheet, with significant excess capital and robust liquidity, enables us to be a pillar of strength, allowing us to consistently serve our clients and communities. The current environment reflects an increasingly complex set of risks. As always, we are prepared for a wide range of scenarios, including the hypothetical 2026 supervisory severely adverse scenario. We continue to serve our clients and communities and invest in products, people, and technology that foster organic growth and promote proper management of our capital. The Board’s intended dividend increase is supported by our consistent investment in our business and strong financial performance. The new share repurchase program provides us with the flexibility to deploy capital in ways that enhance shareholder value over time.”
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase's 2026 DFAST disclosure covers forecasted measures for the nine-quarter 1Q26 through 1Q28 projection period under the Federal Reserve's Supervisory Severely Adverse Scenario, and the results are hypothetical rather than JPMorganChase forecasts.
stress_test_evidence.summary: Important framing: DFAST results are scenario-based and not management's expected forecast.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: The results reflect certain forecasted financial measures for the nine-quarter projection period (1Q26 through 1Q28) under the Supervisory Severely Adverse Scenario prescribed by the Federal Reserve. The stress test has been conducted in accordance with the regulations and other requirements of the Federal Reserve. The results represent hypothetical estimates under the Supervisory Severely Adverse Scenario prescribed by the Federal Reserve on February 4, 2026 and do not represent JPMorganChase's forecasts of actual expected gains, losses, pre-provision net revenue ("PPNR"), net income before taxes, capital, risk-weighted assets (“RWA”), or capital ratios.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: JPMorganChase disclosed that Federal Reserve SCB requirements for large banks, including JPMorganChase, will stay at current levels through September 30, 2027, with revised-model requirements calculated in 2027.
stress_test_evidence.summary: The DFAST disclosure reiterates no new SCB calculation until 2027 under revised models.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: In February 2026, the Federal Reserve announced that the Stress Capital Buffer (“SCB”) requirements for large banks, including JPMorganChase, will remain at current levels through September 30, 2027 with new requirements to be calculated in 2027 based on revised supervisory models that incorporate public feedback. This report does not include any further information on the Firm’s 2026 SCB requirement.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: The DFAST capital-action assumptions exclude common dividends, capital instrument redemptions or repurchases, and common or preferred stock issuances during the projection period.
stress_test_evidence.summary: Standardized DFAST capital assumptions constrain capital actions for stress-test modeling purposes.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: JPMorganChase's results reflect the standardized set of capital action assumptions that are specified in the Federal Reserve's DFAST Rule1 for each quarter of the projection period, as follows: ⚫ No dividends on any instruments that qualify as common equity tier 1 capital (“CET1”); ⚫ Payments on instruments that qualify as additional tier 1 capital or tier 2 capital equal to the stated dividend, interest, or principal due on such instrument; ⚫ No redemption or repurchase of any capital instrument that is eligible for inclusion in the numerator of a regulatory capital ratio; and ⚫ No issuances of common stock or preferred stock
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: Management states that maintaining a strong balance sheet through economic volatility is a strategic imperative for the board, CEO, and operating committee.
stress_test_evidence.summary: The filing emphasizes capital strength as central to strategy and competitive position.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: A strong capital position is essential to the Firm's business strategy and competitive position. Maintaining a strong balance sheet to manage through economic volatility is a strategic imperative of the Firm’s Board of Directors, Chief Executive Officer and Operating Committee.
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.

stress_test_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: a2026_resultsandmethodol.htm
stress_test_evidence.claim: The 2026 severely adverse scenario assumes a severe global recession, including U.S. unemployment peaking at 10.0%, a 58% stock-market decline, a 30% house-price decline, and a 39% CRE-price decline.
stress_test_evidence.summary: Scenario assumptions provide context for evaluating JPMorganChase's stressed capital and loss projections.
stress_test_evidence.excerpt: The Supervisory Severely Adverse Scenario assumes the following stress to key economic variables over a nine-quarter planning horizon: KEY ECONOMIC VARIABLES IN THE SUPERVISORY SEVERELY ADVERSE SCENARIO ⚫ The Firm is also tested against the following add-on components to the 2026 Supervisory Severely Adverse Scenario: ⚫ Global market shock – set of hypothetical shocks to a large set of risk factors which stress trading and certain other fair-valued positions ⚫ Counterparty default – the unexpected default of the Firm’s largest counterparty determined by net stressed losses across derivatives and securities financing transactions ADDITIONAL COMPONENTS1 Key economic variables U.S. real GDP - 4Q25 to trough (4.6%) U.S. unemployment rate - peak 10.0% 3-month Treasury yield - trough 0.1% 10-year Treasury yield - trough 2.3% BBB spreads - 4Q25 to peak 4.7% Stock market index - 4Q25 to trough (58%) House price index - 4Q25 to trough (30%) CRE price index - 4Q25 to trough (39%)
stress_test_evidence.notes: Classified as stress-test/regulatory capital disclosure due to DFAST, SCB, CET1, CCAR, or Federal Reserve stress-test language.
